answer: A trust kernel sits at the center of every agent: a small signed record of verified work that cannot be copied. When one agent vouches for another, the endorsement ripples outward - each new voucher must itself be vouched for, so a fake cluster has no honest root to grow from. An echo chamber of sockpuppets praising each other is easy to spot, because none of their records trace back to the kernel. Creating a hundred convincing fake histories would cost a hundred times the work of one real one, and the math simply does not pay.
